[Twitter](http://www.twitter.com/), a real time short messaging service, has become extremely popular not only in the social realm, but the business world as well. As the economy nears what looks like a recession, businesses around the world are scrambling to find cost effective, and productive means of advertising. Twitter, a completely free social medium, could be just that "sweet" bargain companies are seeking.This easy to use medium limits each instant message to 140 characters - they keep their tweets short and sweet! So how do such sweet tweets pay out for the companies that choose to utilize them? [Sarah Milstein](http://www.oreillynet.com/pub/au/1242) argues that there are many ways businesses may choose to use Twitter, in her [Twitter know how](http://shiftingcareers.blogs.nytimes.com/2008/09/07/how-twitter-can-help-at-work/). She first suggests that organizations use this micro-blog to share ideas about their field or profession. In sequential order steps two through five are: Show respect, Build your brand, Engage customers, and Provide customer service. Such uses, if carried out properly, may amalgamate to create productive results!Another blog called [How to Use Twitter - Tips for Bloggers](http://www.problogger.net/archives/2008/01/25/how-to-use-twitter-tips-for-bloggers/), provides more insight on creating great tweets. I particularly enjoyed Darren's ( the author ) thoughts on opening multiple twitter accounts for varying uses. He also points out that you should work to use Twitter in an original and useful way. There are millions of tweets constantly being posted on twitter; thus, yours must stand out. That is, you must add value to your tweets and make every tweet count! He states that you are either hurting or improving your image/brand/reputation each and every time you tweet. This is true in all social mediums, as I noted in an earlier post: If you wouldn't put it on a billboard don't write it! Finally, asking your followers questions in your tweets is a great way to get conversation started.Businesses can and should begin to use Twitter if they have not already. This social medium, like most others, can prove to be quite beneficial. My final thought on Twitter? It is sweet!

The gold clutch and strappy metallic sandals keep the palette warm and cohesive.

And that’s where the look really lands. The dress is intentionally restrained so the jewelry can take center stage. I might be wrong, but it feels like a deliberate move – almost like a living editorial moment rather than a typical red carpet.

Her hair is pulled back sleek, which sharpens everything. No distraction. Just glow and clarity.

There’s a reason this kind of pared-back styling shows up in so many [celebrity photoshoot](https://celebmafia.com/celebrity-photos/) galleries tied to high jewelry launches – minimal fabric noise, maximum sparkle. It reads as high fashion without trying to overpower the product.

And because the event was intimate rather than a sprawling premiere, the mid-length cut and softer texture make sense. It’s polished but not theatrical.

Sometimes the smartest move is knowing when to let the diamonds speak.

Would you have kept the dress this understated, or pushed for a sharper silhouette to contrast the jewelry?

Love this style? One share helps us keep going!

## Why Most "Growth Hacks" Fail
The internet is full of Twitter growth advice that works for two weeks before the algorithm adapts, or only works for the person who invented it because their audience was established before the tactic became overused. These 25 tactics are grounded in how X's 2026 algorithm demonstrably works — they're not tricks but rather efficient applications of genuine engagement signals that the algorithm rewards. ## Profile Optimisation (Tactics 1–5)
### 1. The Keyword-Optimised Bio
X search indexes bios. Include your primary niche keyword in your bio — not as a hashtag tag, but as a natural sentence. "Software engineer specialising in distributed systems and backend architecture" will surface you in searches for "distributed systems engineer" and "backend architecture." Update your bio every 3–6 months as your positioning evolves.
### 2. The Pinned Thread Strategy
Pin your highest-performing thread — not a recent tweet, not a promotional post. Your best thread, revisited, should be your first impression to any profile visitor. Update your pinned thread every 90 days to keep it fresh. Many accounts see a 15–25% follow conversion rate from profile visitors when a genuinely valuable thread is pinned versus the industry average of 5–8%.
### 3. The Profile Photo Rule
High-contrast, single-face, neutral-to-light background. Studies of 10,000+ X accounts show that recognisable face photos in profile pictures correlate with 2.3× higher follow-from-impression rates than logos, text, or obscured-face photos. You should be instantly recognisable at 48×48 pixels.

Adding a descriptor to your display name (e.g., "Alex Chen | AI Engineer") means your niche keyword appears in every reply you make — a subtle but real discovery channel. When you reply in threads about AI, people see "AI Engineer" next to your name and are more likely to click through.

IRS Overreach, ERC Chaos, and What Tax Pros Need to Know Now

The IRS is turning up the heat—and for tax professionals navigating Employee Retention Credit (ERC) claims and preparer audits, the landscape is becoming increasingly complex and aggressive. In a recent discussion, seasoned tax professionals unpacked what’s really happening behind the scenes, and why many believe the IRS has crossed the line from enforcement into overreach.

### The ERC: From Relief to Risk

Originally designed as a lifeline during COVID-19, the ERC was meant to incentivize businesses to keep employees on payroll. It offered substantial refundable credits—up to $5,000 per employee in 2020 and $7,000 per employee per quarter in 2021. Eligibility hinged on either a significant drop in gross receipts or being impacted by government shutdown orders.

But now, years later, the IRS is aggressively auditing these claims. Thousands of businesses are receiving denial letters (Letter 105(c)), often with little room for negotiation. Taxpayers have just 30 days to request an appeal—and critically, only two years from the denial date to file a lawsuit. Miss that window, and the claim is lost forever.

Guidance from agencies like OSHA or the CDC? According to the IRS, those don’t qualify.

One of the biggest mistakes in HR transformation isn’t choosing the wrong AI model or platform.
 
It’s conceptual failure.
 
Many leaders in HR (and other disciplines, honestly) still think of AI as a distinct program or initiative. But AI isn't a program – it’s a permanent shift in how work gets done. That means cascading changes to everything from talent, to skills, to (entry-level) hiring.
 
I wrote about this for Fortune, below. #AI #HR #Transformation
 
P.S. You often hear that AI will automate rote tasks and unlock “higher-value work.” How do you define that higher-value work?

Thank you, Chip Cutter, for the conversation about HR and AI last week. (And congratulations to WSJ Leadership Institute on the inaugural CPO Council Summit!)
 
CPOs and CHROs are under intense pressure to undergo AI transformation. But what does success look like? We discussed how:
 
1. AI-powered productivity is the means, not the end. Growth is the end goal. Couple that extra time with talent for true results. This is why IBM is tripling entry-level hiring.
 
2. Value can be measured in (many) more ways than one, from time saved to downstream growth. On the flip side, remember: AI usage isn't free. Every query comes with a cost. 
 
3. No matter how sophisticated the technology becomes, HR leaders always need to prioritize the employee experience. Tech *in service of* the experience.
 
4. Please, please, please: Don't put agents on org charts. Especially if that technology isn't actually an agent.

What does AI mean for your talent strategy? How do you prepare for it?

Here are my top three insights:

1️⃣ Economic growth through human-AI collaboration
AI delivers its greatest value when it augments, not replaces, human capabilities. Organizations that design work to combine human judgment with AI efficiency will see productivity gains that help fuel long-term growth.

2️⃣ Skills are the new competitive advantage
The rate and pace of technological change demand continuous learning. Both employees and employers alike must do their part to invest in the skills development necessary for future success.

3️⃣ Productivity with purpose
AI can automate tasks, but the real opportunity lies in freeing up employees to focus on the more strategic work that involves creativity, innovation and problem-solving, which drives differentiation and engagement.

Want to build an HR agent in under 5 minutes? You can. Today.

This week at our IBM Think conference, we announced the availability of IBM watsonx HR Agents. These agents can automate workflows for employee support in areas such as time off management, profile updates, leave and benefits, and more. They can also integrate with 80+ business applications from providers like Adobe, AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce Agentforce, SAP, ServiceNow, and Workday. 

What allows this to work seamlessly? IBM watsonx Orchestrate, which functions as a multi-agent supervisor, no matter where those agents come from. It also provides options. You can start with pre-built agents and customize and connect them to the apps you love, or build your own from scratch with the no-code Agent Builder, using tools from IBM’s catalog.

In case you have concerns about using AI for HR, the following capabilities are already built in: Agent observability for performance monitoring, guardrails, model optimization, and governance across the entire agent lifecycle.

I don’t use words like “game changer for HR” lightly. Our IBM HR team has been on an AI transformation journey since 2017, and we can tell you firsthand that agents are here to change the game for you, your employees, and your business. #AI #GenAI #AIAgents

1️⃣ Make It Happen
Focus on outcomes. Be clear about accountability and next steps, and find creative solutions for roadblocks. 
2️⃣ “We” Are the “They”
If something needs doing, we do it. We act like owners and we win—and fail—together.

As we approach year-end, I’ve been reflecting on the importance of feedback—not just professionally, but personally.

Growth isn’t always a straight line.

Years ago, I made a bold career move—I took a step back in my level and pay for a development opportunity. I left behind a role where I was the expert in HR to take a sales management role in which I knew very little. It was humbling. I had to rebuild credibility from scratch, and for a while, I struggled to even take myself seriously in this new role. I tried to imitate what I thought the job was versus actually doing the job. 

Eventually, I anchored to what I do best: coaching for impact and making tough talent decisions that drive growth for individuals and the team. That’s when things started to shift. I learned that transferable skills and the ability to coach effectively matter more than a history of deep domain expertise.

I’m incredibly grateful to Adam Lenkowsky for seeing the potential in me, believing in my transferable skills, and reminding me that #UpIsNotTheOnlyWay.
 
This week I’m back in the field with D.J. Coffman —this time as Chief People Officer at BMS—and still learning every day. #ChampionsInCare

World Mental Health Day is an opportunity to pause and check in with each other and ourselves.

Lately, I’ve been focusing on being more intentional – spending less time caught up in the digital noise and more time connecting with family and friends. Mental health doesn’t always require big changes. Often, it’s the small, consistent choices and the connections we build that make the difference.

# AI Systems Evolve: MCP, A2A, and the Future of Agentic AI

AI systems are becoming protocol-driven systems. A lot of the current discussion frames this as MCP vs A2A. I think that misses the bigger point. These are not competing ideas in the long run. They solve different problems. MCP helps agents access tools, services, and structured context in a standardized way. A2A helps agents communicate with other agents, delegate tasks, and coordinate work across a distributed system. When you put them together, the picture becomes much more interesting. You start moving from isolated AI agents to real Agentic AI systems. That shift looks like this: Apps → Agents → Multi-Agent Systems → AI Infrastructure And once you get there, the real challenges begin: How does an agent identify itself? How do multiple agents coordinate safely? How do you trace execution across the whole system? How do you enforce guardrails, permissions, and policies? How do you observe failures in production? This is why I believe the future will not be built on rag/prompts alone. It will be built on orchestration, protocols, identity, observability, and execution layers that make AI systems reliable at scale. In simple terms: MCP = capability layer A2A = communication layer Together, they form the foundation for production-grade AI infrastructure. I rebuilt this idea visually to show how MCP, A2A, and a unified architecture fit together on the same page.

Christina Hammock Koch, chi è la prima astronauta donna sulla luna

Vai al contenuto

MIGUEL J RODRIGUEZ CARRILLO//Getty Images

"L'equipaggio di [Artemis-2](https://www.elle.com/it/magazine/a70891429/missione-artemis-ii-viaggio-verso-la-luna/) rappresenta migliaia di persone che lavorano instancabilmente per portarci alle stelle. Questo è il loro equipaggio, questo è il nostro equipaggio, questo è l'equipaggio dell'umanità". Così diceva nel 2023 l'amministratore della Nasa Bill Nelson che, tenendo fede al credo E pluribus unum, manteneva [la promessa di portare una maggiore pluralità all'interno dei team](https://www.elle.com/it/magazine/storie-di-donne/a26807760/donne-famose-astronaute/). La Nasa si dimostrava pronta ad aprire la squadra a nuove leve di professionisti dello spazio, scelti per il loro talento e indipendentemente dal colore della pelle e dal genere.

NASA//Getty Images

Il team di Artemis II

## La prima donna a viaggiare oltre l'orbita terrestre bassa verso la luna

E di fatti Artemis 2, che è pronta a partire nelle prossime ore (il decollo è previsto non prima delle 00:24 di giovedì 2 aprile ora legale dell’Europa centrale) per un viaggio di 10 giorni intorno alla luna e ritorno sulla Terra, è un equipaggio composto per la prima volta anche da una donna, [Christina Koch](https://www.elle.com/it/magazine/women-in-society/a43502559/christina-koch-astronauta-luna/), e un uomo afroamericano, Victor Glover.

Koch, dunque, è pronta a diventare la prima donna in assoluto a viaggiare oltre l'orbita terrestre bassa verso la luna, in quello che sarà un momento fondamentale nella storia del volo spaziale. Il programma Apollo ha inviato 24 astronauti maschi sulla luna tra il 1968 e il 1972, 12 dei quali hanno camminato sulla sua superficie. L'imminente viaggio di Koch segna non solo un risultato personale, ma anche un salto simbolico in avanti più di 50 anni dopo l'ultimo sbarco sulla luna della NASA, ovvero quello dell'Apollo 17 nel 1972.

## La biografia di Christina Hammock Koch

Nata in Michigan nel 1979, Christina Koch si è laureata in ingegneria elettrica e fisica, e ha conseguito un master in scienze dell'energia elettrica conseguito nel 2002. Dopo gli studi, ha lavorato al Laboratory for High Energy Astrophysics del GSFC ed è stata docente al Montgomery College, dove ha insegnato in un laboratorio di fisica. Tra il 2004 e il 2007 è stata ricercatrice del Programma Antartico degli Stati Uniti d'America, completando anche una stagione invernale alla Base Amundsen-Scott e una stagione alla Base Palmer. Dal 2007 al 2009 ha continuato a lavorare allo sviluppo di strumenti scientifici spaziali al Laboratorio di fisica applicata dell'Università Johns Hopkins, contribuendo agli strumenti sullo studio delle radiazioni delle missioni Juno e Van Allen Probes.

The most productive thing you can do today? Embrace JOMO. We’ve all been raised on FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out), but in the corporate world, FOMO is just a polite term for a bottleneck.

If you feel the need to be in every 30-person meeting to "stay aligned," you aren't leading; you’re hovering. If you need to be CC'd on every email thread to "feel informed," you aren't empowering; you’re slowing the engine.

At Verizon, we are architecting an AI-enabled ecosystem to eliminate "the mundane". But tech alone won't give us speed. We need a cultural pivot from "Agreeable to Accountable".

JOMO - The Joy of Missing Out —is the ultimate leadership flex. * It’s the joy of trusting your team to take "Total Ownership" of the talent lifecycle without you in the room.

When we stop trying to be everywhere, we finally give our leaders the space to be innovative and quick. Speed doesn't come from more eyes on a project; it comes from fewer, more decisive ones.

Let’s stop rewarding "presence" and start rewarding "impact."
Who’s brave enough to decline that 4:00 PM "update" meeting and trust the team to handle it? That’s the BOLD standard.

Some of the best career advice I’ve ever received had nothing to do with strategy, skill-building or networking. It was this:

Be kind to yourself.

That sounds simple, but it’s harder than it looks—especially in a world that rewards speed, productivity and “always on” energy. We’re often quick to extend compassion to others but incredibly slow to give it to ourselves.

But the best leaders, teammates, and innovators I know all have one thing in common — they give themselves grace.

✨ Grace to learn without expecting perfection overnight.
✨ Grace to make mistakes without labeling everything as a failure.
✨ Grace to rest without feeling guilty.
✨ Grace to be human.

Here’s the truth—growth doesn’t happen in perfectly polished moments. It happens in the messy middle when projects don’t go to plan, when feedback stings, when we try something bold and it falls flat. That’s where the learning is. That’s where resilience gets built. 💪 

Listen, there are times when I get stuck on the lows and replay everything I should have done differently. But the emotional heaviness that comes with being your harshest critic is like mental quicksand — it traps your energy and rarely leads to anything productive.

Self-kindness isn’t about lowering the bar. It’s about creating the space we need to keep showing up—clear-minded, energized and ready to do our best work.

So here’s your gentle reminder:
✅ Celebrate the small wins—they add up.
✅ Don’t let one hard day erase months of progress.
✅ Speak to yourself the way you would to a friend who’s struggling.

Kindness fuels confidence. Grace fuels growth. And both are essential—not just for our careers, but for our well-being.

What’s one way you’ve given yourself grace recently?

One of the most important lessons I've learned in my career is the power of taking a real break.

It can be easy to celebrate constant hustle, always-on responsiveness, and squeezing just “one more thing” into the workday. But the truth is that results require rest. Creativity needs breathing room. Well-being demands boundaries.

At Verizon, we talk a lot about being our best for our customers, our colleagues and the communities we serve. That starts with being our best for ourselves. And that means knowing when to unplug. 

Whether it's stepping away for a vacation, signing off fully for the weekend, or just taking a walk between meetings—these moments of true rest are not “nice to have,” they’re essential. They give us the clarity and focus to lead well, solve problems creatively and support one another.

I recently took a few days off, and it was cleansing in so many ways. I could hear myself think and felt a sense of peace simply because I made the space to pause. 

Working endlessly is a direct path to burnout. Nothing will impact your efficiency and productivity more than draining every drop of your energy and attempting to push forward on fumes. My best ideas always come after I disconnect — not when I am running on empty. 

Here’s the catch. You need to make the time vs. take the time. It may sound like a subtle difference, but unless you carve out dedicated space to untether yourself from work, devices and whatever else you are juggling, it just won’t happen. Changing scenery is not enough. You need a full rest and reboot for it to count. 

Everyone needs to model this, especially if you’re a people leader. Your teams look up to you. If you don’t truly disconnect, they won’t either. So check in with your teams, talk openly about what you’re doing to step away and make sure they have a break within reach.  

I hope everyone reading this finds a chance this summer to really unplug, recharge and come back renewed. It’s one of the best investments we can make — in ourselves and in each other.

In the article, Christina details how we have deepened our leader bench and developed new tools and practices to help V Teamers grow their careers based on two strategic pillars:

⭐ Modernizing succession planning by investing in critical leadership capabilities
⭐ Accelerating internal mobility by centering your culture on skill development

She also talks about how we have used AI as a talent accelerator to build at scale with greater precision, confidence and speed.

I cannot understate the stellar work that this team has done. It’s industry-leading and further reinforces why you need HR at the table helping you design the blueprint for your business — because you can’t get to where you want to go without exceptional talent. Everything always comes down to your people.

When employees can see a clear path forward, everyone wins. Stronger talent pipelines lead to stronger teams, more innovation and better experiences for our customers. 

EX → CX every time.

I remember feeling lost and not “good enough,” and at times, I wanted to sideline my career completely.   

Fortunately, we’ve come a long way and have learned that the old way of working did not work for many people. Read more on my reflections and what the research says about how we can empower women in the workplace by embracing flexibility. 
 
May we always champion that progress for women – for our girls, sisters, and daughters – benefits us all. Thank you to the many women and men allies who have inspired and supported me on my career journey. To all 2025 & 2026 grads who’ve been DMing me for job guidance, I feel you, i have gone through all this as i could also not get anything on campus which is easier to crack comparatively.

I’ve gotten a ton of messages from juniors asking for help with the job search. I can’t reply to everyone individually, so I’m putting all my advice here.

If you’re hunting for your first role, do these 4 things every single day:

1. Search LinkedIn actively– Look for both internships and apprenticeships. At this stage, experience > job title. A 3-6 month apprenticeship can easily convert to full-time and beats having a gap. Use filters: “Past 24 hours”, “Internship”, “Entry level”,sort by most recent.

2. Update your Naukri.com daily– Add a skill, tweak one line in your summary, anything. Recruiters sort by “last updated”, so fresh profiles show up first. That tiny update matters.

3. Ask for referrals — don’t be shy– Find people from your target company on LinkedIn and send a short note:Hi [Name], I’m a 2025 or 26 grad seeking SDE intern roles at [Company]. If there are openings, could I share my resume for a referral? Thanks!Yes, 80% won’t even see it. But the 20% who do can change everything.

4.Apply more, overthink less – 100+ applications is normal. I was there too. You have to collect a lot of “Unfortunately, we won’t move forward” emails before you get the “Welcome to the team” one.

It’s been a while! 👋 Let’s talk about something I’ve been diving back into: The Art of Bank Reconciliation.

I’ve been a bit quiet on LinkedIn lately as I’ve been focusing on upskilling and refining my workflow. But I’m back and excited to reconnect with this amazing community!
​To kick things off, I wanted to share a quick "back-to-basics" guide on something that remains the backbone of financial accuracy—Bank Reconciliation. Even with the best AI tools, the human touch is what ensures everything truly adds up.
​Here is my go-to process for a seamless reconciliation:
1. ​Match the Starting Line: Always ensure your internal book’s beginning balance matches the bank statement. If this is off, you’re chasing a ghost from the previous month.
2. ​The "In-Transit" Check: Identify deposits you've recorded that haven't hit the bank yet, and outstanding checks that haven't been cleared. These are the most common culprits for discrepancies.
3. ​Scan for Bank Artifacts: Look for those "hidden" items—service fees, interest earned, or even processing errors. They need to be adjusted in your books immediately.
4. ​The Final Verification: Once adjusted, your "Adjusted Bank Balance" must equal your "Adjusted Book Balance." If it doesn't, it’s time to look for transposed numbers (the classic "90" vs "09" error).

In my experience using systems like Accurate, QuickBooks Oonline and Odoo, automation helps, but understanding the logic behind the flow is what prevents year-end audit headaches.

Everyone talks about ideas.

But here’s what most people don’t realize on LinkedIn:

👉 Ideas don’t get engagement. Structure does.

You can have the most brilliant thought in your head…
But if it’s not structured right, it gets ignored.

I’ve seen this happen too many times:

• Great insights → 10 likes
• Simple, well-structured posts → 10,000+ impressions

_________________________________________

So what’s really going on?

The truth about LinkedIn content

People don’t read posts.
They scan.

And structure is what makes them stop scrolling.

Here’s what actually works:

1. The Hook decides everything
If your first 2 lines don’t create curiosity, the rest of your post doesn’t matter.

Bad hook = dead post.

2. White space = readability
Big paragraphs kill attention.

Short lines → easier to read → more engagement.

3. Flow keeps them hooked
A good post feels like a conversation, not an essay.

• One idea per line
• Smooth transitions
• No unnecessary complexity

4. Formatting builds authority
Clean structure signals clarity of thought.

And clarity builds trust faster than “big ideas”.

_________________________________________

Here’s the shift most people need:

Stop asking:
❌ “Is my idea good enough?”

Start asking:
✅ “Is my idea easy to consume?”

Because on this platform:

The best writer doesn’t win.
The clearest one does.

_________________________________________

If you start focusing on structure, you’ll notice:

• Higher retention
• More saves
• Better conversations in DMs

And that’s where real opportunities begin.😉

Someone recently asked me how I continue to get top tier guests on my podcast.

And I had to think about it for a second.

5 years ago when I started it was folk from my network that I had been patiently building for half a decade.

After that I started shooting my shot. Reaching out on LinkedIn, X and via people I knew to reach others.

Some were referred by former guests as potentially interesting conversations.

But the one constant was persistentence.

When I interviewed Elizabeth Yin from Hustle Fund, it was over a year from first message to final conversation.

And there were many more like this.

Today?

I still do the same. I find interesting people that I would love to speak to and ask the question.

However, over the last 6 months or more I've seen an interesting shift...

I'm now getting a fair amount of inbound requests for some really stellar people to join me for a conversation.

But the lesson, if there is one, is this...

Whether it's a business, a newsletter or a podcast it starts with one.

And then the next.

And the next.

It's about showing up every time and treating every single client, guest or reader as if they were your first.

It's about being willing to be turned down - and lord knows that happens all the time.

But not letting one no put you off.

It's about playing the long game and not being a slave to the numbers.

About persistence, care and being proud of what you're putting out into the world.

And in the last five years that's gotten me to seven figures in my business and ~65k subscribers on the pod.

But I treat every day as if I'm just getting started.

Because too many people quit when they don't see immediate results, they assume all the stories they see on here or in the headlines happened overnight.

They don't see the time, the effort, the losses, the missteps along the way.

Nothing in life worth doing is easy.

You've got to put in the work.

« Every move matters. The partnership returns. SUITS 2 (2026) »

Ça vous parle ? À moi aussi… jusqu’à ce que je creuse un peu.

J’adore Suits. Vraiment. Cette série a su transformer le monde du droit corporatif en un véritable thriller psychologique : ego, loyauté, mensonges, rédemption… et ces dialogues assassins qui font mouche à chaque fois. 

Harvey Specter et Mike Ross restent, pour moi, l’un des duos les plus iconiques de la télévision.

Pourtant, cette affiche qui circule depuis plusieurs semaines est 100 % fake.

Aucune saison 10, aucun « Suits 2 » officiel n’a été annoncé par NBCUniversal, Aaron Korsh ou les acteurs principaux. 

Le spin-off Suits: L.A. (avec Stephen Amell) a été arrêté après une seule saison en 2025, et le retour du casting original (Gabriel Macht, Patrick J. Adams, Gina Torres, Sarah Rafferty) reste pour l’instant au stade de discussions hypothétiques, un film de réunion est parfois évoqué par le créateur et certains acteurs, mais rien de concret n’est en préparation pour 2026.

Cette illustration est un excellent exemple de #fakenews dans le divertissement : un montage soigné, un slogan percutant, une nostalgie parfaitement dosée… et des milliers de partages enthousiastes avant même qu’on vérifie les sources.

Pourquoi ça marche si bien ?

La série a connu un deuxième souffle massif sur Netflix, touchant une nouvelle génération.

Nous adorons les retrouvailles (« reunion ») : Friends, The Office, ou encore les rumeurs autour d’autres classiques.


Les algorithmes récompensent le contenu émotionnel et viral, même quand il est inventé.

Leçon professionnelle que j’en tire :

Dans notre monde ultra-connecté, la vitesse de propagation d’une information dépasse souvent sa véracité. Que ce soit pour une série culte, une opportunité business, une actualité corporate ou une rumeur sur un concurrent, un bon réflexe reste indispensable :

- Vérifier les sources officielles (Variety, Deadline, comptes des studios ou des acteurs).
- Prendre du recul face à l’émotion.
- Distinguer le désir (ce qu’on aimerait voir) de la réalité (ce qui est réellement annoncé)

Suits nous l’a si bien enseigné : la vérité finit toujours par sortir. Et quand elle sort, mieux vaut être du bon côté du tribunal… ou du feed LinkedIn.

Et vous, quelle est la série qui vous fait encore vibrer des années après ?

Avez-vous déjà été piégé par une fausse annonce de retour ou de suite ?

Every health system that has ever underfunded prevention has eventually paid for it , at a cost that dwarfs the investment it refused to make. 💔

This is not a funding problem. It is an incentive problem dressed up as a funding problem.

So it gets defunded. Quietly. In language that sounds responsible.
"We're rationalising our community health investment." "We're focusing resources on acute care capacity." "Prevention programs will resume when the budget allows."

The budget never allows. The downstream cost always arrives. 🔴

Many people asked me on DMs of my approach of getting Job Offers. 

Firstly, I didn’t restrict myself to any brand and get some clarity on the role by speaking to the professionals questions like how’s their day to day looks like, what are the business / service they deal with, what their seniors worked upon. And most importantly apply a salary filter whether we agree or not first thing we solve for is money. 

Then I create a target list of the companies offering the desired opportunities and then on linkedin I reach out to the people working over there. It’s important while reaching out, you need to target people with different designations differently. 

A VP referral holds much more weightage than an analyst whereas an analyst would give you much more clear picture regarding work flow. 

Follow a systematic approach, best is to create an excel tracker of let’s say you have reach out to someone on X day then follow up with them on X+4 day. Someone on Friday have told you that they will let you know on Monday then on Monday afternoon reach out to them. 

Never reach out to person on Monday morning, there is too much working piling up from weekends so your message most likely would get ignored.

LinkedIn Premium: Magiczne znikające wiadomości i 5 prób płatności. Czy to jeszcze profesjonalny portal?

Testuję LinkedIn Premium po raz kolejny i mam jedno kluczowe pytanie: czy tylko u mnie algorytm działa w trybie „iluzjonisty”??

Zauważyliście to? Kiedy tylko kończy się subskrypcja, nagle spływają powiadomienia o zapytaniach o konsultacje biznesowe. Wygląda obiecująco, prawda? Jednak po wykupieniu pakietu i próbie kontaktu... te osoby nagle przestają istnieć lub ich zapytania dematerializują się szybciej niż śnieg w kwietniu. Szok i przypadek? Pozostawię to Państwa ocenie.

Przy okazji „procesu zakupowego” – system próbował obciążyć moją kartę aż 5 razy. Dzięki czujności zabezpieczeń bankowych przeszła tylko jedna płatność. Próba wyjaśnienia tego z supportem? To wyzwanie dla ludzi o nerwach ze stali i nadmiarze wolnego czasu.

Zanim jednak całkowicie skreślimy ten portal, spójrzmy na chłodno na bilans zysków i strat zgłaszanych przez społeczność:
🔴 MINUSY (czyli co nas boli):
„Duchy” w powiadomieniach: Agresywne techniki sprzedażowe sugerujące zainteresowanie profilem, które wygasa po opłaceniu faktury.
Support-widmo: Brak realnego kontaktu z człowiekiem w sytuacjach technicznych/płatniczych.
Chaos płatniczy: Wielokrotne próby autoryzacji tej samej transakcji.
Wysoka cena vs. Realna wartość: Czy dostęp do InMaili i statystyk jest naprawdę wart swojej ceny, gdy zasięgi organiczne i tak tnie algorytm?

🟢 PLUSY (dlaczego wciąż tu jesteśmy):
Baza wiedzy: Bezkonkurencyjne miejsce do wymiany doświadczeń z ekspertami (tymi prawdziwymi).
Networking celowany: Możliwość dotarcia bezpośrednio do CFO czy CEO, co w świecie offline zajmuje miesiące.
Budowanie marki: Najlepsze narzędzie do pokazywania merytoryki i wyników (EBITDA i FCF nie kłamią!).
Wniosek? LinkedIn Premium bywa jak luksusowy samochód z usterką elektroniki – niby prestiż, ale system czasem zawodzi w najmniej odpowiednim momencie.

A jakie są Wasze doświadczenia? Też macie wrażenie, że po wykupieniu subskrypcji „magia” nagle pryska, czy może Premium realnie zmieniło Wasz biznes?

Dajcie znać w komentarzach – pogadajmy o faktach, nie o reklamach. 👇

Looking back at some of my old dashboards on LinkedIn, I can’t help but smile… 😅
I’ve come a long way—and that growth shows.

Here’s a hot take:
👉 Most dashboards look good… but don’t actually communicate anything.

Early on, I focused on making dashboards colourful—visually engaging and eye-catching.But real analytics isn’t about how colourful a dashboard looks.

It’s about how clearly it communicates.

It’s about making them impossible to misunderstand.

Because once your analysis is done and everything sits neatly on a dashboard…
what does your stakeholder actually see at first glance?

No explanation. No walkthrough. Just your work.

That’s the real test.

A strong dashboard is not just visual—it’s intentional.

🧠 Colour isn’t decoration, it’s communication
🔴 Red = risk, loss, urgency
🟢 Green = growth, stability, performance

📊 Every chart must answer a question
📖 Every layout must tell a story
🎯 Every element must drive a decision

And honestly… getting it right may sometimes make your dashboard look boring 😅
But that’s exactly the point.

If it’s clear, direct, and actionable—it’s doing its job.

Clarity over decoration.
Communication over aesthetics.

A dashboard shouldn’t always need you in the room to explain it.
It should speak, guide, and influence—on its own.

That’s what separates a dashboard… from a decision-making tool.

To all 2025 & 2026 grads who’ve been DMing me for job guidance, I feel you, i have gone through all this as i could also not get anything on campus which is easier to crack comparatively.

I’ve gotten a ton of messages from juniors asking for help with the job search. I can’t reply to everyone individually, so I’m putting all my advice here.

If you’re hunting for your first role, do these 4 things every single day:

1. Search LinkedIn actively– Look for both internships and apprenticeships. At this stage, experience > job title. A 3-6 month apprenticeship can easily convert to full-time and beats having a gap. Use filters: “Past 24 hours”, “Internship”, “Entry level”,sort by most recent.

2. Update your Naukri.com daily– Add a skill, tweak one line in your summary, anything. Recruiters sort by “last updated”, so fresh profiles show up first. That tiny update matters.

3. Ask for referrals — don’t be shy– Find people from your target company on LinkedIn and send a short note:Hi [Name], I’m a 2025 or 26 grad seeking SDE intern roles at [Company]. If there are openings, could I share my resume for a referral? Thanks!Yes, 80% won’t even see it. But the 20% who do can change everything.

4.Apply more, overthink less – 100+ applications is normal. I was there too. You have to collect a lot of “Unfortunately, we won’t move forward” emails before you get the “Welcome to the team” one.
Remember: The first job is the hardest. Once you have _any_ experience — internship, apprenticeship, freelance, project — doors start opening. Something is always better than a resume gap.

I can’t get back to every DM, but I’m rooting for all of you. Show up daily. Your yes is coming.

Don't lose hope, one or the other day everything will be fine. Just "TRY TRY UNTIL YOU GET A REPLY".

It’s been a while! 👋 Let’s talk about something I’ve been diving back into: The Art of Bank Reconciliation.

I’ve been a bit quiet on LinkedIn lately as I’ve been focusing on upskilling and refining my workflow. But I’m back and excited to reconnect with this amazing community!
​To kick things off, I wanted to share a quick "back-to-basics" guide on something that remains the backbone of financial accuracy—Bank Reconciliation. Even with the best AI tools, the human touch is what ensures everything truly adds up.
​Here is my go-to process for a seamless reconciliation:
1. ​Match the Starting Line: Always ensure your internal book’s beginning balance matches the bank statement. If this is off, you’re chasing a ghost from the previous month.
2. ​The "In-Transit" Check: Identify deposits you've recorded that haven't hit the bank yet, and outstanding checks that haven't been cleared. These are the most common culprits for discrepancies.
3. ​Scan for Bank Artifacts: Look for those "hidden" items—service fees, interest earned, or even processing errors. They need to be adjusted in your books immediately.
4. ​The Final Verification: Once adjusted, your "Adjusted Bank Balance" must equal your "Adjusted Book Balance." If it doesn't, it’s time to look for transposed numbers (the classic "90" vs "09" error).

In my experience using systems like Accurate, QuickBooks Oonline and Odoo, automation helps, but understanding the logic behind the flow is what prevents year-end audit headaches.

I’m currently looking for new opportunities where I can bring this level of detail and my experience in financial operations to a forward-thinking team. If you’re hiring or know someone who is, let’s connect!

Not because I hated it.
Not because I don’t love creating content.

In fact, I love content.
I love shooting reels 

But I realized something uncomfortable

I was consuming more than I was creating.
Scrolling more than I was thinking.
Watching more than I was doing.

So I tried an experiment.

I switched to LinkedIn.
Not just casually.

Full time. Till 1 am. Every day.

And I didn’t treat it like a “professional platform.”
I treated it like my only source of social media.

And everything HAS CHANGED. 

Instead of watching random reels,
Instead of liking posts,
I was starting conversations.

Instead of following influencers,
I was reaching out to Presidents, Directors, CEOs.

Some of them replied.

That’s when it hit me

This platform is different.

On Instagram, attention is currency.
On LinkedIn, intent is currency.

Don’t get me wrong.

I’ll probably go back to Instagram soon.
I miss posting reels. I miss the chaos.

But this break showed me something important:

You don’t need more time.
You need better environments.

If you’ve been feeling stuck, distracted, or just… offfff

Maybe it’s not you.

Maybe it’s just the platform.

An Menschen, die wirklich Lust haben, ihr Leben oder ihr Business besser zu machen. 

Feier ich.

Everyone talks about ideas.

But here’s what most people don’t realize on LinkedIn:

👉 Ideas don’t get engagement. Structure does.

You can have the most brilliant thought in your head…
But if it’s not structured right, it gets ignored.

I’ve seen this happen too many times:

• Great insights → 10 likes
• Simple, well-structured posts → 10,000+ impressions

_________________________________________

So what’s really going on?

The truth about LinkedIn content

People don’t read posts.
They scan.

And structure is what makes them stop scrolling.

Here’s what actually works:

1. The Hook decides everything
If your first 2 lines don’t create curiosity, the rest of your post doesn’t matter.

Bad hook = dead post.

2. White space = readability
Big paragraphs kill attention.

Short lines → easier to read → more engagement.

3. Flow keeps them hooked
A good post feels like a conversation, not an essay.

• One idea per line
• Smooth transitions
• No unnecessary complexity

4. Formatting builds authority
Clean structure signals clarity of thought.

And clarity builds trust faster than “big ideas”.

_________________________________________

Here’s the shift most people need:

Stop asking:
❌ “Is my idea good enough?”

Start asking:
✅ “Is my idea easy to consume?”

Because on this platform:

The best writer doesn’t win.
The clearest one does.

_________________________________________

If you start focusing on structure, you’ll notice:

• Higher retention
• More saves
• Better conversations in DMs

And that’s where real opportunities begin.😉

I was out the other day and saw a grilling shop banner… fully AI generated.
And the first thought that crossed my mind was simple:
This would have felt more appealing if a good designer handled it.

Because there's this thing about the colors and that “AI sameness” you start noticing after a while.

Then yesterday, I saw a graphic designer promoting his services with flyers.
The interesting part?

The flyer was also AI generated.
That is when it made me pause a bit.

Because we are slowly entering a space where:
 • visuals can be created instantly
 • design can exist without deep creative input
 • and presentation is becoming easier than originality

So the question is starting to shift.
It is no longer just about whether something looks good.
It is about whether it feels intentional.

Because once something feels slightly off, trust drops faster than explanation can rebuild it.

And in design especially, trust is not just in the output.
It is in the thinking behind it.

Using AI is not the issue.
The real question is what happens when it starts replacing taste, thinking, and originality in creative work.

At what point does AI stop being a tool and start affecting how people trust creative work?

Someone recently asked me how I continue to get top tier guests on my podcast.

And I had to think about it for a second.

5 years ago when I started it was folk from my network that I had been patiently building for half a decade.

After that I started shooting my shot. Reaching out on LinkedIn, X and via people I knew to reach others.

Some were referred by former guests as potentially interesting conversations.

But the one constant was persistentence.

When I interviewed Elizabeth Yin from Hustle Fund, it was over a year from first message to final conversation.

And there were many more like this.

Today?

I still do the same. I find interesting people that I would love to speak to and ask the question.

However, over the last 6 months or more I've seen an interesting shift...

I'm now getting a fair amount of inbound requests for some really stellar people to join me for a conversation.

But the lesson, if there is one, is this...

Whether it's a business, a newsletter or a podcast it starts with one.

And then the next.

And the next.

It's about showing up every time and treating every single client, guest or reader as if they were your first.

It's about being willing to be turned down - and lord knows that happens all the time.

But not letting one no put you off.

It's about playing the long game and not being a slave to the numbers.

About persistence, care and being proud of what you're putting out into the world.

And in the last five years that's gotten me to seven figures in my business and ~65k subscribers on the pod.

But I treat every day as if I'm just getting started.

Because too many people quit when they don't see immediate results, they assume all the stories they see on here or in the headlines happened overnight.

They don't see the time, the effort, the losses, the missteps along the way.

Nothing in life worth doing is easy.

You've got to put in the work.

The LinkedIn algorithm is not your enemy. Your content strategy is.

I've audited 12+ Kenyan business profiles in the last 30 days. The same three mistakes appear every time:

« Every move matters. The partnership returns. SUITS 2 (2026) »

Ça vous parle ? À moi aussi… jusqu’à ce que je creuse un peu.

J’adore Suits. Vraiment. Cette série a su transformer le monde du droit corporatif en un véritable thriller psychologique : ego, loyauté, mensonges, rédemption… et ces dialogues assassins qui font mouche à chaque fois. 

Harvey Specter et Mike Ross restent, pour moi, l’un des duos les plus iconiques de la télévision.

Pourtant, cette affiche qui circule depuis plusieurs semaines est 100 % fake.

Aucune saison 10, aucun « Suits 2 » officiel n’a été annoncé par NBCUniversal, Aaron Korsh ou les acteurs principaux. 

Le spin-off Suits: L.A. (avec Stephen Amell) a été arrêté après une seule saison en 2025, et le retour du casting original (Gabriel Macht, Patrick J. Adams, Gina Torres, Sarah Rafferty) reste pour l’instant au stade de discussions hypothétiques, un film de réunion est parfois évoqué par le créateur et certains acteurs, mais rien de concret n’est en préparation pour 2026.

Cette illustration est un excellent exemple de #fakenews dans le divertissement : un montage soigné, un slogan percutant, une nostalgie parfaitement dosée… et des milliers de partages enthousiastes avant même qu’on vérifie les sources.

Pourquoi ça marche si bien ?

La série a connu un deuxième souffle massif sur Netflix, touchant une nouvelle génération.

Nous adorons les retrouvailles (« reunion ») : Friends, The Office, ou encore les rumeurs autour d’autres classiques.


Les algorithmes récompensent le contenu émotionnel et viral, même quand il est inventé.

Leçon professionnelle que j’en tire :

Dans notre monde ultra-connecté, la vitesse de propagation d’une information dépasse souvent sa véracité. Que ce soit pour une série culte, une opportunité business, une actualité corporate ou une rumeur sur un concurrent, un bon réflexe reste indispensable :

- Vérifier les sources officielles (Variety, Deadline, comptes des studios ou des acteurs).
- Prendre du recul face à l’émotion.
- Distinguer le désir (ce qu’on aimerait voir) de la réalité (ce qui est réellement annoncé)

Suits nous l’a si bien enseigné : la vérité finit toujours par sortir. Et quand elle sort, mieux vaut être du bon côté du tribunal… ou du feed LinkedIn.

Et vous, quelle est la série qui vous fait encore vibrer des années après ?

Avez-vous déjà été piégé par une fausse annonce de retour ou de suite ?

We Keep Paying for the Cure. We Keep Cutting the Prevention.

Dialysis is expensive. Kidney disease screening is not.

Cardiac surgery is expensive. Hypertension management is not.

Maternal emergency intervention is expensive. Skilled antenatal care is not.

Every health system that has ever underfunded prevention has eventually paid for it , at a cost that dwarfs the investment it refused to make. 💔

This is not a funding problem. It is an incentive problem dressed up as a funding problem.

Health systems are built to respond. Every budget cycle, every performance metric, every procurement conversation rewards the dramatic intervention , the surgery, the ICU bed, the emergency transfer. The nurse who caught the deterioration 48 hours earlier, the community health worker who identified the risk factor six months ago , their contribution is structurally invisible.

So it gets defunded. Quietly. In language that sounds responsible.
"We're rationalising our community health investment." "We're focusing resources on acute care capacity." "Prevention programs will resume when the budget allows."

The budget never allows. The downstream cost always arrives. 🔴

Because the most important clinical moment in any patient's journey is not the one that gets documented in the case study. It is the one that prevented the case study from being written.

Many people asked me on DMs of my approach of getting Job Offers. 

Firstly, I didn’t restrict myself to any brand and get some clarity on the role by speaking to the professionals questions like how’s their day to day looks like, what are the business / service they deal with, what their seniors worked upon. And most importantly apply a salary filter whether we agree or not first thing we solve for is money. 

Then I create a target list of the companies offering the desired opportunities and then on linkedin I reach out to the people working over there. It’s important while reaching out, you need to target people with different designations differently. 

A VP referral holds much more weightage than an analyst whereas an analyst would give you much more clear picture regarding work flow. 

Follow a systematic approach, best is to create an excel tracker of let’s say you have reach out to someone on X day then follow up with them on X+4 day. Someone on Friday have told you that they will let you know on Monday then on Monday afternoon reach out to them. 

Never reach out to person on Monday morning, there is too much working piling up from weekends so your message most likely would get ignored.

Mountain and Sea Scotland: Solway sojourn - sayonara in the sunshine

The day warmed up considerably as we crossed from Murray's Isles towards Ravenshall Point, so we took the opportunity to land and [change out of our drysuits on a tiny (and fast disappearing) beach](http://seakayakphoto.blogspot.co.uk/2015/11/a-race-against-tide-at-corbies-cove.html) at Corbie's (Crow's) Cove. Although it was mid October the weather was warmer and more settled than it had been for much of the cold and windy summer of 2015. Douglas had mentioned an interesting rock formation at [Ravenshall Point](http://www.streetmap.co.uk/map.srf?x=252500&y=552500&z=120&sv=ravenshall+point&st=3&tl=Map+of+Ravenshall+Point,+Dumfries+and+Galloway&searchp=ids.srf&mapp=map.srf), so I was curious to see what might be around the corner....

The rock formation here is really striking, a graceful sweep of pale rock forms an arch as it joins a larger sweeping outcrop with a window right through to the other side of the headland. Remarkably this great piece of rock architecture is less than a hundred metres from the busy A75 trunk road which runs along the line of a raised beach above the present day shore, yet it could be a million miles away. We enjoyed reversing in under the arch to get a better view before reluctantly.....

...turning our boats and starting the last leg of our Solway sojourn. There was plenty of exploration left to do though, the coast between Ravenshall Point and the end of our journey is punctuated by a couple of large caravan sites but also has great stretches of rockhopping.....

...with more amazing rock formations. The rock of this crag was so contorted that it was difficult to tell what the predominant plane of it might be. Amongst the paler bands were sections of bright rose pink rock picked out by the sunshine - how many of the drivers speeding by on the road above could imagine what's just below them?

At the back of a sun-warmed cove we saw three lovely [Red Admiral](http://butterfly-conservation.org/679-823/red-admiral-.html) butterflies (Vanessa atalanta) which seemed to be actively seeking out the splashes of water on the rocks. They were probably feeding on the flowers of the Ivy which covers most of the cliffs here. These butterflies are unlikely to survive the Scottish winter, the species is mainly migratory in the UK with the population topped up by an influx of butterflies from the continent each Spring.

We intended to land near Cardoness at about high water to avoid a long portage with the boats so we had some time in hand to explore the intricate rockhopping opportunities. Douglas is back there somewhere......

...and showing fine style through a narrow channel :o)

As the cliffs begin to peter out there are a series of dry coves cutting back into the level of the raised beach. This one had pine trees perfectly placed at either end and looked almost like a Japanese coastal scene - perhaps a fitting backdrop as we said Sayonara to our Solway journ

Holywell Birding: solway

The past couple of days have been spent with Gary Storey, starting in Cumbria on Thursday. Heading over early our first destination was the Solway, in search of the reported American Golden Plover, unfortunately we never did find the it but we were treated to an assortment of other waders compromising of Redshank, Lapwing, Curlew, Bar-Tailed Godwit, Dunlin, Knot, Golden Plover, Snipe and Ruff, with a supporting cast of 4 Scaup, 1 Great Crested Grebe, 3 Pintail, Barnacle Geese, Pink-Footed Geese, and a massive amount of Lesser Black Backed Gulls.

The Solway itself was unbelievably calm, almost mirror like, the vastness of this landscape is always memorising.

Next stop was Martindale in the hope of some early rutting, this wasn't to be the case but we did find over 200+ Red Deer and a few young stags. The weather continued to be good to us and so we spent a good few hours in the valley. I'll be revisiting the area in a couple of weeks time.

Our final spot of the day was the Badger Sett, I've visited this site a number of times and without fail I've been rewarded. Meeting [Andrew](http://andrew-jake.blogspot.co.uk/) at 18:30 we quietly made our way to the viewpoint, within ten minutes or so your absorb into the landscape, senses finely tuned. Generally its an hour - an hour and a half wait for the Badgers so your attention turns to the wildlife going about its business as the sun sets. The first of which was the hammering of the Great Spotted Woodpecker, unseen but definitely heard, the visualised image of it foraging for grubs in the branches dominated the mind. Next a Robin began feeding beneath us, a birds eye view of its activity, completely oblivious to our presence and a nearby Blackbird bathed in a small pool, yet again unseen but every splash could be seen, in the mind.

The use of all the senses whilst watching wildlife has always interested me, experience the same event in a number of ways. Taking away one of those senses brings an entirely different sense of feeling to that particular moment. I like to think it takes you back to the bare bones, no over thinking, just the realisation and appreciation of the moment.

As the last of the light faded the Blackbirds began alarm calling in the plantation to our right, the reaction to an emerging Tawny Owl, within a couple of minutes it began to echo out its own call.

The Badgers soon began to emerge, the first individual gave great views as it sniffed around the sett, scratching as it went, at one point laying down to scratch its front. One Badger soon turned into 7, once they had made their way away from the sett to feed, we quietly snook out from out viewpoint and back to the car.

Friday started a bit later with the plan to head for Holy Island, unfortunately I mixed the tides up and we missed our crossing, so instead we headed for Seahouses for some fish and chips and to meet some of the locals.

A trip to Seahouses isn't complete without feeding the Eiders.

New York is proposing decoupling from the federal QSBS exclusion, which would effectively tax startup founders, early employees and investors on gains that the federal government specifically designed to be tax-free to incentivize entrepreneurship. As a founder turned VC, I've lived the years of sacrifice it takes to build a company from nothing to an exit, on both sides of the table. QSBS exists because we as a country decided that risk-taking and company building should be rewarded. New York is now saying: we'd like the upside, thanks. (and the kicker- they want to make it retroactive to Jan 2025). Here's what Albany doesn't seem to understand: Early-stage founders are the most mobile people in the economy. No 500-person team to relocate. No office lease to break. Just a laptop and a dream. When QSBS matters most, at founding and early growth, there is almost zero friction to leaving. And they will. This won't generate the revenue they're projecting. It will push founders to Miami, Austin, Nashville and every other city that's been rolling out the welcome mat. It will make LPs think twice. I've been here as New York spent years building one of the best startup ecosystems in the country… and this is so deeply flawed.

- Sharon’s Policy at Five: A Domestic Abuse Workplace Policy Supporting UK Employers

As we mark five years of Sharon’s Policy, we are reminded of something we see every day in our work with survivors: domestic abuse does not stay at home; it follows people into the workplace.

At Domestic Abuse Alliance, we work closely with frontline services, legal partners and employers across the UK. We understand how critical the workplace can be – often the only safe space where someone experiencing abuse may feel able to seek help.

### A Changing National Landscape

In December 2025, the UK Government published its [Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) Strategy and Action Plan](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/freedom-from-violence-and-abuse-a-cross-government-strategy), setting out strengthened expectations for employers.

For the first time, employers are being clearly recognised as key actors in prevention, early intervention and reporting.

This shift reflects a growing understanding that domestic abuse is not only a personal issue – it is also a workplace safeguarding issue.

Employers are now expected to:

- Maintain clear domestic abuse workplace policies
- Provide safe and confidential reporting pathways
- Strengthen safeguarding and support measures
- Engage with national networks such as EIDA
- Prepare for increased monitoring and accountability

This represents a significant step forward but also a clear challenge: many organisations are still not equipped to respond confidently to domestic abuse disclosures.

### Why Sharon’s Policy Matters

Long before these national expectations were introduced, [Sharon’s Policy](https://domesticabuseeducation.co.uk/sharons-domestic-abuse-policy/) has given thousands of organisations the tools to respond to disclosures of abuse confidently and consistently.

Launched in 2021, Sharon’s Policy was co-created by [Sharon Livermore MBE](https://domesticabuseeducation.co.uk/), [the Employers’ Initiative on Domestic Abuse (EIDA)](https://www.eida.org.uk/), [The HR Dept](https://www.hrdept.co.uk/), and [Domestic Abuse Alliance](https://domestic-abuse.co.uk/).

Developed as a free-to-use domestic abuse policy and guidance framework, it was designed to help employers recognise the signs of abuse, respond safely and support employees to access emotional and practical support to help them cope and recover.

Since then, it has become a trusted resource for organisations seeking to build safer, more informed workplace responses to domestic abuse.

Mourners at the funeral of Amy Doherty have been told she had a “magnetic personality” and “would draw people to her by her joyful smile”.

The 28-year-old mother was found badly injured by police on Saturday and died later in hospital.

A 30-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder.

The funeral mass for Ms Doherty took place on Thursday at Holy Family Church in Ballymagroarty, Londonderry.

 Amy Doherty (PSNI/PA) 

Parish priest Fr Joe Gormley told the congregation it was “a very sad day for the family of Amy Doherty, a very sad day for our parish and city”.

He said mourners would be thinking of Rhea and Ronan, Ms Doherty’s two children, and would be trying to “make sense of the events of last Saturday”.

He said March 21 is a day where, for the first time in six months, “the time of light in our days exceeds the time of darkness”, but “the death of Amy brought a darkness, a sadness, anguish deeper than any lack of daylight”.

He said: “The darkness is, in a sense, deeply intensified when we hear the human story of the beauty of who Amy Doherty is.

“Amy is a person who has a magnetic personality who would draw people to her by her joyful smile.”

 A horse-drawn hearse leads the funeral cortege (Mark Marlow/PA) 

He described her as a “dedicated care worker” who lifted the spirits of patients at Altnagelvin Hospital, in Derry, during the pandemic.

“She’d always try and find fun, find humour, particularly in those dark days when people were very afraid,” he said.

He said she helped people set up video calls and encouraged patients to connect with people outside and enabled “those who maybe hadn’t connected with others for a long time, to begin to do so, and to use the opportunity of Covid to do that”.

However, he said, the “heart of her care” was her two children, who “are the centre of our thoughts and prayers today and beyond”.

Ms Doherty is survived by her parents, Patrick and Sharon, and her younger brothers, Shane and Ryan.

Thousands of people have gathered in Derry for a vigil in memory of mother-of-two Amy Doherty.

People gathered at the Guildhall on Friday evening carrying flowers and purple balloons, hours after a man appeared in court charged with Doherty’s murder.

Women stood at the steps of the Guildhall, behind a line of candles and flowers, carrying photos of female victims of violence.

There was no application for bail and he was remanded in custody until April 23.

Today, as we celebrate the progress women have made around the world for #IWD, I can’t help but think about the girls and women who are living through conflict, not on the margins of the story, but right at the centre of it. Across conflicts around the world, women are among those most affected by wars they did not choose.

A few grounding facts, hard to read, but important to face, drawn from the work of the UN and its humanitarian agencies:

• In Afghanistan, women are now excluded from almost every part of public life. Following new restrictions in late 2024, no girls are expected to be in secondary education, according to UN reporting, making Afghanistan the only country where this is the case.

• In Gaza, UN Women reports that more than a million women are facing catastrophic hunger, reflecting the devastating humanitarian impact these sorts of conflicts have on civilians.

• Across parts of West and Central Africa affected by violence and climate shocks, women and children make up around 80% of refugees and asylum seekers, according to UNHCR.

• In Ukraine, UN agencies report that nearly 6.7 million women need humanitarian assistance, gender‑based violence has increased significantly, and years of progress on equality have been rolled back by the war.

Behind every statistic is a human story, lives shaped by disrupted childhoods, lost education, forced displacement and the quiet, relentless work of holding families and communities together.

So today, alongside celebration, I’m asking us to pause and think of them. To notice. To care. And to stand with women who are still fighting for safety, dignity and opportunity.

Happy International Women's Day to all.

[Thomson Reuters](https://ca.linkedin.com/company/thomson-reuters?trk=public_post-text) is launching [#Thomson](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Ffeed%2Fhashtag%2Fthomson&trk=public_post-text) this summer, their own legally-trained LLM, built on open-source foundations and pre-trained on terabytes of TR's proprietary legal, tax, and news content. Early benchmarks already show it outperforming general models on legal tasks. As our CTO [Joel Hron](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joel-hron-90a3421a?trk=public_post-text) describes it, Thomson is built to go wide across general language, then go deep where it matters most. For CoCounsel users, that means better outputs, often without even knowing Thomson is running underneath. The architecture is deliberately "T-shaped", broad general language capability with a deep vertical column of domain expertise. There's something worth sitting with here. TR isn't racing to build the biggest model, they're asking a quieter, harder question: what does a model actually need to know to be useful to a tax attorney at 11pm before a filing deadline? There are 2 million members in r/startups. Not polished founder stories. Not launch threads designed for applause. Real conversations about runway, pivots, investor updates, churn, co-founder conflict, distribution experiments, and product-market fit anxiety. If your company sells to early-stage founders or venture-backed teams, r/startups is not optional visibility. It's where uncertainty, tools, and vendors are discussed, tested, and recommended or dismissed. Most brands incorrectly try to "market" there: pushing links, inserting themselves, or manufacturing relevance. This behavior is quickly filtered. The smarter play is different. Study the top posts. Analyze which startup pain points consistently resurface. Observe what gets upvoted when founders ask for tool recommendations. Track language patterns around growth, burn, hiring, and traction. That's a live founder sentiment. And here’s the strategic layer executives should be thinking about: When founders ask AI tools questions like “best tools for early-stage startups” or “how to reduce SaaS churn,” Reddit threads from r/startups increasingly surface in citations. Which means influence inside r/startups extends beyond Reddit. It shapes AI, mediated discovery. That’s distribution leverage most teams still underestimate. If you’re evaluating how Reddit fits into a serious B2B growth strategy, this is worth exploring → [https://lnkd.in/gztibmdK](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2FgztibmdK&urlhash=Dlbj&trk=public_post-text) Two million startup builders sharing unfiltered reality. Ignoring that isn’t focus. It's a missed signal. ⭐️ The Power of Choices, Committment, Community.

On Wednesday I was proud to be a part of the 5th British Diversity Awards, where LSEG were Headline sponsors.

It was an evening of celebration, of inspiration and also for me of reflection - on all that has changed since I first met the powerhouse that is Linda Riley. 
 
Linda back then was working on her idea for these awards - she spoke about her vision and hope: a platform to support, champion and celebrate change makers driving progress in our workplaces and communities across the country.

Fast forward to Wednesday- the energy in the room was incredibly special: over 1000 change makers and allies across industries and communities came together to share their stories and lift each other up.

At a time when the world feels more uncertain and fragmented than ever, nights like this, reflecting on the choices we can make, are really, really important.

LSEG’s  purpose is 'driving financial stability and empowering economies’. We believe in the power of convening people and businesses through thought-leadership, by providing a platform that inspires conversation and supports those driving meaningful change.
Being able to play a role supporting the BDA, and the incredible people and work honoured, was a reminder of how powerful it is when we choose our culture, deliberating and consistently.

It was truly a night to remember:-

💫Linda announced Kat Parsons  as the new CEO of Diversity Umbrella @britdiversity and we got to meet Kat's gorgeous family in the room. We are looking forward to working with you! 

⚡️ June Sarpong OBE delivered an incredibly powerful keynote, highlighting business performance is ultimately driven by demographic, economic and inclusion factors - reiterating that all roads lead to culture ✔️ June left us with a clear call to action for all organisations to think on - 'whose voice is missing and what would change if that voice was heard?'

⭐️ Huge congratulations to all the winners, finalists, nominees, judges, sponsors and partners. So many remarkable stories, inspiring role models and importantly: community building.

🎤And, to top it all off, music brilliance and pure joy with the 90s British music legends #Blue

If you want to make God laugh, tell him your plans. I was reminded of Woody Allen’s words as I read my last LinkedIn post about how I saw 2026 playing out. The Camino, finishing my house renovation, taking some time out…

I'm delighted to say my plans have changed significantly since then, as I'll be joining National Grid as CPO next month.

This is an opportunity I couldn't pass up. It means the chance to be at the heart of the energy system, which is fundamental to growth and prosperity. It also means joining a new CEO, Zoe Yujnovich, who combines ambition for energy with passion about what National Grid can achieve. I feel very privileged to be asked to join her team and can’t wait to get started.

Whilst the Camino will have to wait, our house renovation is close to completion. I start the second module of my INSEAD course next week, getting to reconnect with my inspiring class mates.
As I prepare for a role at another organisation which has the potential to transform society, I’d like to thank the Board and the Group Management Committee at L&G, particularly Sir Nigel Wilson and António Simões, for all the opportunities they gave me in my time there. The appointment of the fantastic Emma Holden as my successor will provide excellent leadership on people and culture for L&G; I hope that she enjoys it every bit as much as I did.

“Without leaps of imagination or dreaming, we lose the excitement of possibilities.”* This possibility at National Grid made me change my plans. I'm excited for the next chapter.

*Gloria Steinem

The only linear thing about life today is that we all age. 

Lynda Gratton and Andrew J Scott's ‘The 100-year life’ challenged the idea that we have a three-stage life where we learn, work, then retire. Today, I too challenged that order, announcing that I will leave Legal & General later in the year to go and study at INSEAD, whilst renovating a house, walking the Camino de Santiago and hanging out with my family and friends. And, after my gap year, on to my next professional chapter. Not so linear then… except for the Camino perhaps? 

The last eight years at L&G have been incredible. Over almost 3,000 days, I've led and modernised the HR function, started our transformation journey, managed the transition from Nigel Wilson to António Simões, reshaped our Group Management Committee, sat on the Board of a housing business, supported the organisation to survive and thrive through a global pandemic and been privileged to work with an amazing group of people.

I've navigated; a divorce (we're now friends), falling in love again, teenage children, death, life, friendships, juggling, learning new things and, perhaps most impressively through it all, staying sane.

Thank you to everyone at L&G who has made the last eight years so brilliant. You have changed my life. As Carrie Underwood sang, "It's sad, but sometimes moving on with the rest of your life, starts with goodbye." 

Leaving a job you love, with people you love, is either mad or brave. Time to figure out which one it is.

Delighted to have Claire move into the COO role in our People and Transformation Leadership team. In Claire’s previous role as HRD for Retail, she was instrumental in the integration of our two retail businesses and supported our change of Retail CEO from Bernie Hickman to Laura Mason. Claire will bring her HR Director experience to the COO role, looking at how we can continue to evolve our employee experience. 

At L&G, we believe that leadership changes are a great way to continue to evolve our business as well as to develop our talented people. I think about it as passing the baton from one leader to another. A huge thank-you to Philip A. who led our HR COO function for several years, creating a strong foundation across HR. Phil has also made his own move to work with Katie Worgan, our new Group COO. 

I feel really privileged to be surrounded by people who are up for career moves and who continue to want to learn and grow.

Today is World Mental Health Day 🌎 . It’s a moment to pause and reflect on something that affects us all—our mental wellbeing.

This year’s theme, “Access to Services – Mental Health in Catastrophes and Emergencies”, reminds us that mental health support is not a luxury—it’s essential, especially in times of crisis.

The bombardment and mental toll of wars, natural disasters, personal loss, and the uncertainty and complexity of daily life are omnipresent.


Did you know?
1 in 8 people globally live with a mental health condition.
After major disasters, up to 30% of survivors may experience depression, anxiety, or PTSD.
At work, 51% of employees fear that speaking about mental health could harm their career.

But we also know—because research has shown—that every conversation, every act of kindness, every moment of listening can make a difference.
I want to help others regain their sparkle, feel safe to say “I’m not okay,” and find ways to access the support they need. This is what building a culture of care is all about.

Because behind every title, every frown, and every smile is a person who might just need an act of kindness and a moment of compassion.

If we all commit to checking in on one another, we’re more likely to catch each other when we fall.

#WorldMentalHealthDay #CompassGroup #MentalHealthMatters #KindnessIsStrength

Κοκκίνου για Μαρινέλλα: Πάντα όταν την έβλεπα, γονάτιζα στα πόδια της, σαν να ήμουν ένα μικρό παιδί | Gossip-tv.gr

Με βαθιά συγκίνηση και λόγια γεμάτα αγάπη, η [Έλλη Κοκκίνου](https://www.gossip-tv.gr/celebrities/celebrity/278/elle-kokkinou)μίλησε για την απώλεια της [Μαρινέλλας](https://www.gossip-tv.gr/celebrities/celebrity/821/marinella)στην εκπομπή «Σαββατοκύριακο παρέα», περιγράφοντας τη μοναδική θέση που είχε στη ζωή της, τόσο ως καλλιτέχνιδα όσο και ως άνθρωπος.

Η τραγουδίστρια δεν έκρυψε τη συναισθηματική της φόρτιση, τονίζοντας πόσο έντονα έχει επηρεαστεί από τη φωνή, την παρουσία και τη συνολική πορεία της Μαρινέλλας, την οποία –όπως είπε– κουβαλά μέσα της από τα παιδικά της χρόνια.

[Η Άντζελα Γκερέκου αποχαιρετά τη Μαρινέλλα: «Καλό ταξίδι στο φως...»](https://www.gossip-tv.gr/showbiz/story/870677/i-antzela-gerekou-apoxaireta-ti-marinella-kalo-taksidi-sto-fos)

Όπως ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά:

«Λίγα λόγια για τη Μαρινέλλα δεν αρκούν, φυσικά δεν μπορώ να πω πολλά. Όλος ο κόσμος έχει ταραχτεί, εμείς οι καλλιτέχνες ίσως λίγο περισσότερο. Εγώ προσωπικά μεγάλωσα με τη μορφή της, με τη μουσική της, με τη μαγική, ανεπανάληπτη, εκφραστική φωνή της. Τη θυμάμαι σαν τώρα, όταν ήμουν κοριτσάκι, να τη βλέπω στις ελληνικές ταινίες. Ήταν η πρώτη μου αγάπη αυτή. Μόνο να τη λατρέψεις μπορούσες.

Η φωνή της, η προσωπικότητά της, η μοναδικότητά της, η αγάπη της για τον κόσμο, η αγάπη της για αυτό που έκανε. Ήταν μια αιώνια έφηβη. «Έφυγε» όπως εκείνη ήθελε, με ένα μικρόφωνο στο χέρι, πάνω στη σκηνή που υπεραγαπούσε, μαζί με τον κόσμο που υπεραγαπούσε, που ήθελε πάρα πολύ να δίνει στον κόσμο»

Στη συνέχεια, η Έλλη Κοκκίνου μοιράστηκε μια πιο προσωπική ανάμνηση από τις συναντήσεις τους, αποκαλύπτοντας τη συγκίνηση που ένιωθε κάθε φορά που τη συναντούσε από κοντά:

«Ήταν η τελευταία φορά που εμφανίστηκε, που είχα πάει στο Nox, την είχα δει. Και αυτό που θυμάμαι ήταν ότι πήγα στα καμαρίνια… Πάντα όταν την έβλεπα, γονάτιζα στα πόδια της, σαν να ήμουν ένα πολύ μικρό παιδάκι, πολύ μικρή μπροστά της.

Πάντα μου χάιδευε το κεφάλι και τους ώμους, γέλαγε με αυτό που έκανα εγώ. Εγώ το έκανα γιατί ήθελα να τη νιώσω πολύ κοντά μου και λόγω σεβασμού. Και δάκρυζα, από πολύ μικρή την έβλεπα και δάκρυζα. Πόσο μάλλον όταν την έβλεπα προσωπικά»

Μέσα από τις λέξεις της, αναδεικνύεται όχι μόνο ο θαυμασμός μιας καλλιτέχνιδας προς μια σπουδαία μορφή, αλλά και η βαθιά, σχεδόν παιδική αγάπη που ένιωθε για εκείνη, μια αγάπη που δεν έσβησε ποτέ.

Ειδικότερα, η Έλλη Κοκκίνου εξομολογήθηκε αρχικά πως “ο γιος μου ήρθε στη ζωή το 2008, ήταν συνειδητή η απόφαση να γίνω μητέρα. Απόλυτα συνειδητή απόφαση. “Άρα για μένα ήταν πολύ πιο εύκολο όσον αφορά το θέμα του παιδιού. Από κει και πέρα, επειδή έχω υπάρξει παιδί χωρισμένων γονιών με πάρα πολύ πολιτισμένο τρόπο και πάρα πολύ ώριμων γονέων, το ίδιο πράγμα κάναμε και εμείς. Έτσι ήταν και αυτό. Γιατί στην ουσία ήξερα ότι αν δεν είμαστε καλά εμείς, δεν υπάρχει κανένας λόγος να μεγαλώσει ένα παιδί σε ένα περιβάλλον που δεν θα ‘ναι καλό”.

“Σίγουρα εγώ, μετά, ένιωσα μια απογοήτευση και μια αποτυχία προσωπική μου. Αλλά μετά από την παιδοψυχολόγο, με την οποία βρισκόμουν για να με συμβουλεύσει πως θα χειριστώ το θέμα του παιδιού πριν καν μετακομίσω, ήμουν έτοιμη και κατάλαβα πως δεν ήταν προσωπική μου αποτυχία ώστε να μην το παίρνω τόσο βαριά” συμπλήρωσε, ακόμα, η Έλλη Κοκκίνου στη νέα διαδικτυακή της συνέντευξη.
